page: Microsoft Azure D64lds_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dldsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

This server includes 3780 GB of local NVMe storage and is premium storage capable. In benchmark testing, the D64lds_v6 demonstrates strong performance across multiple domains. It achieves a top-tier result in static web serving throughput at 97.56 GB/sec and image processing. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 4425.91 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 109.18 GB/sec. Multi-threaded operations are robust, as evidenced by a bzip3 decompression rate of 369.2 GB/sec and a PassMark CPU score of 70905.37.

The D64lds_v6 is designed for compute-heavy workloads that do not require high memory-to-CPU ratios, making it a cost-efficient choice for raw processing power. The inclusion of AMX instructions enables strong performance in CPU-based machine learning, with LLM prompt processing reaching 39.92 tokens/sec for a 70B model. The 3780 GB of local disk space, combined with strong database operation benchmarks of 31925.83 on PassMark and Redis SET performance of 83.04 million operations per second, makes this instance highly suitable for high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and database indexing.
description: Microsoft Azure D64lds_v6 is a compute-optimized, low-memory virtual machine powered by a 64-vCPU Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 128.0 GB of RAM and 3780 GB of local NVMe storage. The system excels in compute-intensive tasks, leveraging Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions to deliver strong performance in software compilation, cryptography, and CPU-based LLM inference. Benchmark results highlight top-tier capabilities in static web serving at 97.56 GB/sec and image processing, alongside strong multi-threaded decompression and database operations. This hardware profile offers a cost-efficient solution for high-throughput processing and database workloads that require substantial local storage but do not demand high memory density.
